transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-25
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 49 minutes (scheduled 09:00 PT)
Location: Zoom
Attendees (recorded):
- Maya Chen (Redwood AE)
- Ethan Park (Redwood SE)
- Priya Rao (Redwood CSM)
- Dr. Lila Hart (Hartwell Labs, CTO)
- Marco Ruiz (Infra Lead)
- Sofia Nguyen (Head of ML)
- Evan Cole (Security)
- Tara Lim (PM)
- Speaker 2 (intern, joined late)

Summary:
Quick implementation/immersion kickoff for Hartwell Labs' pilot of Redwood Private (VPC) for inference of internal therapeutics research assistant. Primary concerns: network/VPC setup, data residency, SSO/SAML, auditing/KMS, latency profile for low-latency RAG (retrieval-augmented generation) flows. Agreed next steps: runbook + VPC checklist, customer to send traffic profile, Redwood SE to propose benchmark plan and instance sizing.

Topics covered:
- Onboarding timeline and success criteria
- Network design (VPC peering, egress) and IP allowlisting
- Security: SAML SSO, KMS/HSM, SOC 2 questions
- Pilot scope: 2-week pilot, 100k tokens/day peak sim
- Tradeoffs: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (they want Private/VPC but asked about canary fallback)
- Observability: token-level cost, trace IDs, alerting

Action items (quick list presented on call):
- Redwood: runbook draft, perf plan, pilot playbook
- Hartwell: CIDR ranges, traffic examples, stakeholder contact for security review

Questions captured:
- Can we do SAML with our Okta? (yes, standard SAML flow)
- How will KV cache be handled across nodes? (Ethan: continuous batching + prefix caching, note: sometimes transcribed as KV cash)
- What are the SLAs during pilot vs production? (Priya: pilot best-effort, Dedicated has SLA)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: Okay folks, thanks for joining. I'm Maya from Redwood, I'm the AE on this account. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Lila: Hi, Lila here. Thank you.
[00:10] Marco: Marco — infra.
[00:12] Sofia: Sofia, ML.
[00:13] Ethan: Ethan, SE — I'll drive the perf and infra bits.
[00:16] Priya: Priya, CSM.
[00:18] Evan: Evan, security.
[00:19] Tara: Tara, PM.
[00:20] Speaker 2: (muffled) yep, here.

[00:30] Maya: Great. Quick agenda: go over pilot goals, runbook and timeline, security and VPC details, perf benchmarking, then next steps. Any additions?
[00:38] Tara: Maybe a short section on who approves go/no-go on the customer side.
[00:40] Maya: Good, we'll add that.

[01:05] Maya: Lila, can you share the success criteria from your side — what would make this pilot a win?
[01:12] Lila: Sure. For us the big items are: predictable latency under 200ms p50 for single-turn queries, ability to guarantee data doesn't leave our AWS region, and audit logs for all requests for 90 days. Also SSO integration for our platform team. If those are met we can expand to a 3-month prod rollout.
[01:35] Ethan: Quick clarification — when you say 200ms p50, is that including the RAG retrieval latency? Because retrieval can add 80-120ms depending on your store.
[01:44] Sofia: We mean total, retrieval included. We do a local vector store so should be low.
[01:48] Ethan: Okay, got it. We'll model with a sim that includes a 50ms retrieval to start.

[02:15] Marco: On the network side, we need to understand how Redwood will route traffic. We prefer Private with a VPC conn, not public hosted. Also we have strict egress controls — admin wants to allow only specific AWS endpoints.
[02:28] Maya: Totally. For Private we have a customer VPC peering pattern or PrivateLink depending on your cloud. We can do VPC peering + NAT egress restrictions. We'll send the VPC checklist.
[02:38] Evan: About KMS — will Redwood integrate with our CMK? We need HSM-backed keys for token storage at rest.
[02:44] Priya: We support KMS integrations, and for Private we can tie into customer-managed keys. I'll share our KMS integration doc.

[03:10] Sofia: Any limitations with larger context windows? We're exploring 16k windows for some flows.
[03:16] Ethan: Runtime supports large context but performance varies; for 16k we recommend model quantization and tuned batching. Also we'll suggest hardware profile with more memory. We'll propose a quantized variant for the pilot so cost stays reasonable.

[03:52] Lila: We are also sensitive about model variants — we want to pin to an open model family, but fallback is OK if the model isn't available.
[03:59] Maya: Yes, pinning is supported; and routing policies can fallback to a compatible variant. We'll document that in the rollout playbook.

[05:05] Ethan: On caching, small note — we have prefix caching and KV cache sharing but if you have bursty seqs there can be cache warm-up. The transcript generator sometimes writes KV cash, please ignore that little typo.
[05:20] Marco: (laughs) Kv cash, got it.

[06:00] Tara: Timeline — we're aiming to run the pilot in mid-October, ideally week of Oct 11. Is that feasible?
[06:10] Maya: Yes, reasonable. We'll need your CIDR ranges and Okta SAML metadata by end of month to get VPN/VPC and SSO configured.
[06:17] Marco: We'll pull that together.

[07:00] Evan: A couple security questions: do you provide per-request audit IDs, and can we ship logs to our SIEM?
[07:08] Priya: Yes — we emit trace IDs and can forward audit logs via secure syslog or S3 with lifecycle. For Private we can push logs into your S3. I'll add SIEM integration notes.
[07:20] Evan: How about redaction? Some tokens could contain PHI in our test dataset.
[07:26] Priya: We have configurable redaction hooks and can run pre-token filters as part of the ingestion pipeline. We'll work with you on a policy for the pilot.

[08:10] Sofia: For the pilot workload, we plan two flows: 1) short single-turn answers from internal docs, 2) 3-turn RAG conversation with context length ~6k. We'll try to simulate 100k tokens/day peak.
[08:24] Ethan: Great. For the perf plan I'll run two sims: a latency-focused sim and a throughput sim. I'll include a model variant matrix and suggested GPU types.

[09:00] Lila: About cost — we need a rough estimate for the pilot and for steady-state. Can you provide an amortized per-token cost with both quantized and fp16 options?
[09:10] Maya: Yes, we'll provide a pilot cost sheet. Quick note: Dedicated and Private unit economics differ; Private often has a baseline infra/ops fee plus usage. We'll include ballpark numbers in the follow-up.

[10:00] Marco: Any constraints on break-glass fallback to hosted if our VPC connectivity breaks?
[10:06] Ethan: Yes we can configure a fail-open to Redwood Hosted for short windows, but it's opt-in and noted in the runbook. We'll also add monitoring alerts and automatic cutover rules.

[11:15] Tara: Who signs off on go/no-go? On our side Tara (PM) will do feature gating, Lila will do security sign-off, Marco will confirm infra readiness.
[11:26] Maya: Noted. On our side Maya will coordinate, Priya is your CSM for ops, and Ethan handles SE bench.

[12:40] (brief pause while someone screenshares a runbook template)
[12:45] Priya: I'm pulling up the onboarding runbook template now. It covers access, network, SSO, KMS, data flows, perf plan, and rollback. I'll share after the call.
[12:55] Lila: Perfect.

[14:00] Sophia: Small aside — how are model updates handled during pilot? We don't want automatic updates.
[14:06] Ethan: You can pin a model version and we won't auto-roll. For security patches to runtime we have scheduled maintenance windows. We'll note policy in the runbook.

[15:20] Marco: Regarding observability, we need token-level cost breakdown and per-route latency. Is that available in console for Private?
[15:28] Maya: Yes, the Redwood Console ships metrics for Private as well; per-route dashboards and trace IDs are available. Some retention options are an add-on.

[16:05] Lila: About retention — we need logs kept for 90 days. Is there an extra fee?
[16:10] Priya: There's an add-on for extended retention; we'll include options.

[17:00] Tara: Can you walk through the exact pilot scope one more time? Who is responsible for what?
[17:06] Maya: Sure: Redwood provides runbook, config templates, SE will run perf sims and a smoke test harness. Hartwell provides CIDR, Okta metadata, sample prompts, and test dataset. Security does the review. After two-week pilot we'll collect metrics and decide go/no-go.

[19:45] Evan: A note that we'll require a pen-test before production ramp; pilot can be limited scope but pen-test schedule needs discussion.
[19:53] Maya: Understood, we'll coordinate.

[21:00] Sofia: One more perf nuance — some of our prompts are very long and we might need streaming tokens. Does Redwood support streaming responses across Private?
[21:06] Ethan: Yes, streaming is supported. We'll test streaming latencies in the perf plan.

[23:30] (crosstalk)
[23:34] Speaker 2: question about where to upload test keys?
[23:36] Priya: We'll send secure upload instructions (S3 with encryption) — don't upload to public channels.

[26:10] Maya: All right, to recap next steps: Priya shares runbook and SAML/KMS docs by 09/28, Ethan shares perf plan and instance recommendations by 10/02, Hartwell sends CIDRs, Okta metadata, example prompts by 09/30, we schedule pilot window week of 10/11.
[26:35] Lila: Sounds good.

[27:00] Marco: Small nit — can the pilot simulate nightly batch jobs? We occasionally run large batch scoring overnight.
[27:08] Ethan: Yes, we'll include a nightly batch throughput test and show an alternative instance mix.

[29:50] Tara: One final ask — please include an escalation matrix for on-call during the pilot.
[29:55] Maya: We'll include that in the runbook.

[31:10] (wrap-up, minor pleasantries)
[31:20] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and a calendar invite for the pilot prep.
[31:26] Lila: Thanks all.
[31:30] (meeting ends, some participants linger)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-heard words (e.g., Kv cash, VPCe) and some speaker labels auto-filled. Internal timing markers approximate.
